keyFindings.description: tmux strips a trailing ';' from an argv token (command separator; '\;' is the literal). Candidate 'HOME;' from a continuation line 'HOME;=…' -> show-environment -g 'HOME;' runs as '… HOME' -> exit 0 -> confirmed -> set-environment -g -u 'HOME;' runs as '-u HOME' -> the real allow-listed HOME is removed from the global table; log records 'HOME;'. Reproduced through the real scrub (deep audit) and at the has/-u level (me) on scratch 3.7c servers. Siblings: 'plain;' -> 'unknown variable: plain' != expected -> throw -> boot refusal; ';' alone -> exit 0 then 'too few arguments' throw. Second shape: trailing whitespace — candidate 'key ' (from 'key = value') -> tmux echoes 'unknown variable: key \n'; line 103 trims stderr only -> mismatch -> throw -> boot refusal whose message names a value fragment (parent entry already unset, so the supervisor's next boot succeeds). Neither reachable from a PEM or a bash function body; both need a raw multi-line value with such a continuation line; production has none. Fix (local): escape a trailing ';' as '\;' in both argv sites (verified tmux echoes the literal back exactly) and compare stderr with only the final newline stripped (or trim both sides); tests: 'key = value' line refused/not thrown/not -u'd; 'HOME;=x' with HOME in paneEnv refused, HOME never -u'd; 'X;' as a real entry confirmed and unset under its own name. Alternative (structural): parse `show-environment -s` — entries close on an unescaped '"; export <NAME>;' matching the opener; exact names, zero probes, no fragments in tmux's own show-messages log (deep audit finding 4), no 66x2 tmux calls.

'Both secrets children run with the same stripped environment as private_key_command minus SECRETSD_SESSION_TOKEN_FILE' — inherited #1017 wording not reconciled by the rebase: private_key_command now runs on the daemon's own unstripped process.env (config.ts:553-557; L105 says so), stripDispatchEnv is gone. Say: both secrets children run under the daemon's own process.env, like private_key_command, minus exactly SECRETSD_SESSION_TOKEN_FILE (the LEGION-77 learning L59-61 already has it right).

'read only by private_key_command, the one child that runs under the daemon's own process.env on purpose' — PR-authored; since #1017 runSecretsGet (config.ts:579-586) is a second such child. Name both.
